Summarise environmental values around observations

Source: R/extract_to_buffer.R
extract_to_buffer.Rd

Calculate one summary per observation and variable within horizontal, depth and/or temporal windows. Combine complementary netCDF sources before assessing coverage. Observations and input order are retained.

Usage

extract_to_buffer(
  data,
  nc,
  var = NULL,
  horizontal_radius_km = 0,
  lon_cell_radius = NULL,
  lat_cell_radius = NULL,
  depth_radius_m = 0,
  depth_layer_radius = NULL,
  time_before = 0,
  time_after = 0,
  time_unit = c("days", "hours", "minutes", "seconds", "months", "years"),
  statistic = "mean",
  weighting = c("weighted", "equal"),
  min_valid_fraction = NULL,
  infer_bounds = FALSE,
  method = NULL,
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  depth_col = "depth",
  date_col = "date",
  id_col = NULL,
  file_col = "file",
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  time_resolution = c("auto", "datetime", "daily", "monthly", "yearly"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  spatial_match = c("within", "nearest"),
  max_distance_km = NULL,
  output_col = NULL,
  return_match_info = TRUE,
  quiet = FALSE,
  target_col = NULL,
  max_target_difference = NULL,
  target_ties = c("NA", "lower", "higher")
)

Arguments

data

Observation table, matrix, named list or sf POINT object.

nc

netCDF path, paths, opened ncdf4 connection, list, or file table.

var

Variable name or vector of names. NULL detects one data variable per file, excluding referenced bounds and coordinate variables.

horizontal_radius_km

Horizontal geodesic radius in kilometres. Positive radii below 10000 km are supported.

lon_cell_radius, lat_cell_radius

Optional integer radii in grid cells. A radius of one on both axes requests a 3 by 3 neighbourhood. Mutually exclusive with a positive horizontal_radius_km.

depth_radius_m

Symmetric depth radius in metres, positive downward.

depth_layer_radius

Optional integer radius in physical depth order. Mutually exclusive with a positive depth_radius_m.

time_before, time_after

Non-negative temporal distances before and after the observation. Both use time_unit.

time_unit

One of days, hours, minutes, seconds, months or years. Days are 24 elapsed hours. Months and years require whole numbers and shift the UTC calendar, clamping to the destination month's last day.

statistic

One of "mean", "sd", "se", "min", "max" or "most_similar". SD uses the sample variance correction. SE is SD divided by the square root of the effective sample size. Min and max ignore weight magnitudes.

weighting

"weighted" uses intersecting area, thickness and duration; "equal" gives equal weight to valid samples. Coverage uses physical support in both modes. A point-selected axis contributes a factor of one.

min_valid_fraction

Minimum valid fraction of the entire requested support, between zero and one. NULL uses 0.8 for summaries and zero for most_similar (any valid support). Empty/all-missing buffers remain NA.

infer_bounds

Allow missing bounds to be estimated using neighbouring coordinate midpoints, with half-gap extrapolation at outer edges. Inferred depth support is clipped at zero metres. A singleton needs explicit bounds.

method

Depth selection on an unbuffered vertical axis: nearest, surface, bottom or 2d. NULL uses 2d without a depth axis and nearest with one. Leave NULL when requesting a depth interval or layer neighbourhood.

lon_col, lat_col, depth_col, date_col

Observation coordinate columns. Dates are required only for temporal variables. Date and ISO date-only text centre time buffers at midnight UTC; POSIXt preserves instants.

id_col

Optional observation identifier column used in diagnostics.

file_col

File-path column when nc is a table.

lon_dim, lat_dim, depth_dim, time_dim

Optional netCDF dimension overrides.

time_match, time_resolution, max_time_diff

Point-time selection options on an unbuffered time axis; see extract_to_point(). max_time_diff is in days and cannot be combined with a temporal window.

spatial_match, max_distance_km

Point-cell or index-seed selection options; see extract_to_point(). They do not expand a kilometre buffer.

output_col

Output name for one variable, or a named character vector mapping multiple variable names to distinct output columns.

return_match_info

Add a list column named _match_info per variable, containing coverage, source, bounds and selection diagnostics.

quiet

Hide explanatory summaries. Time-zone and ambiguous-location warnings remain active.

target_col

Column containing the numeric target for most_similar. For several variables, a named variable-to-column mapping. Targets must use the environmental variable's units. Original NA targets return NA.

max_target_difference

Optional non-negative maximum absolute difference from the target, in the environmental variable's units.

target_ties

How to resolve equally similar different values: NA (default), lower or higher. Repeated identical winning values retain all their locations in match_info; no file is chosen by input order. This rule does not choose locations among repeated identical values.

Value

The normalised observation table with one numeric summary column per variable and, optionally, a diagnostic list column per output. sf inputs retain their geometry. Existing columns are never overwritten. most_similar always adds _match_lon, _match_lat, _match_depth and _match_time (UTC). They describe winning model coordinates, not corrected observations. Ambiguous or unavailable fields are NA. Longitude/latitude are returned together only for a unique horizontal location. All winning records remain in match_info when requested. Unresolved value or location ties emit one bounded warning per output with affected rows and guidance.

Support and limitations

For normalised weights p, corrected variance is sum(p * (x - mean)^2) divided by sum(p * (1 - p)); effective sample size is 1 / sum(p^2). Equal weighting reproduces ordinary sample SD and SE. SD and SE require at least two valid samples; otherwise they return NA with a diagnostic. SE assumes independent samples and does not correct spatial or temporal autocorrelation. It is not an automatic estimate of environmental uncertainty. All statistics, including min and max, require the requested valid coverage.

At least one window must be positive. Bounds describe represented support; inferred intervals do not establish that instantaneous values are interval means. The calculation treats each sample as constant over its assigned support. No interpolation or nearest fallback expands an empty buffer.

Geographic grids must have separable one-dimensional longitude and latitude axes. Circles are geodesic on WGS84 with 720 segments. Each cell is weighted by the area of the circle it covers, measured on the WGS84 ellipsoid with terra. This is a polygonal approximation, independent of sf_use_s2(). Unsupported projections, calendars, climatologies or transformed vertical coordinates require explicit preprocessing.

Complementary sources are combined before applying min_valid_fraction. Overlapping selected support is an error, including duplicate values or a missing copy. Sources for one variable must use matching value units. Point-time selection is resolved across eligible sources before aggregation. Index neighbourhoods require matching grid/layer coordinates and bounds across sources. If requested indices extend beyond available coverage, the result is NA because the full requested physical support is unknown.

See also

extract_to_point(), extract_to_area()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
observations <- data.frame(lon = 0, lat = 38, depth = 60,
                           date = as.Date("2020-01-15"))
extract_to_buffer(observations, "temperature.nc", var = "thetao",
                  horizontal_radius_km = 5, method = "surface")
extract_to_buffer(observations, "temperature.nc", var = "thetao",
                  depth_radius_m = 10, time_before = 3)
} # }
